issues.body: schedule_crons filters out any non-mapping entry or non-string cron and returns [] for a non-list schedule. Consequently schedule_minute_map skips an entirely malformed scheduled lane, or derives a partial minute set when one entry is valid and another malformed. That contradicts the module's fail-closed contract: the omitted declaration is precisely the evidence consumers need to know is unreadable. The comment claiming callers can get a refusal from cron_minutes is incorrect because filtered entries never reach cron_minutes. The self-tests at lines 313-318 explicitly require the unsafe skip/empty behavior, so they prevent detection rather than covering the failure mode.
issues.fix_hint: Make schedule_crons distinguish an absent schedule from a declared malformed schedule. Raise CronMapError (or another consistently handled refusal) when schedule is not a list, an entry is not a mapping, or cron is not a string; then add hermetic schedule_minute_map tests showing both an all-malformed lane and a mixed valid/malformed lane raise instead of producing an absent or partial map. Update the current permissive self-test rows accordingly.
issues.title: Malformed schedule declarations are silently omitted from the derived map

verdict.summary: The extraction introduces a fail-open parse boundary in the new shared trust-plane helper. Although the module promises that an unreadable cron/workflow cannot disappear from the derived map, schedule_crons silently filters malformed schedule entries and silently treats a non-list schedule as absent. schedule_minute_map therefore can return a plausible partial map (or omit the lane entirely) for a workflow GitHub will not run, allowing collision/rate assertions to go green on incomplete evidence. The self-test currently codifies this permissive behavior. This is a new major finding relative to round 1's clean approval, so progress is regressing.
